one_line: British magistrate in North India whose observations and telegraph reports framed early warnings during the 1857 rising.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, lean but sturdy build, upright posture suggesting bureaucratic discipline and field experience.
appearance.face: Oval face, light fair complexion tanned by the sun, straight nose, neatly trimmed sideburns, calm grey-blue eyes with a thoughtful gaze, default expression alert and analytical rather than harsh.
appearance.hair: Short, tidy dark brown hair parted to the left, slightly wavy at the front, worn without facial hair except narrow sideburns to mid-ear, topped with a lightweight cream-coloured colonial sun helmet (early pith hat) with a brown leather chin strap resting loose under the jaw.
appearance.costume: Mid-1850s British civil officer attire adapted to North India: a well-fitted light khaki cotton tunic-length coat reaching mid-thigh with two breast pockets and dark brown buttons, worn over a crisp white shirt with a modest standing collar; dark olive green straight-cut trousers slightly loose for riding, tucked into mid-calf brown leather riding boots; a narrow dark brown leather belt at the waist holding a small pouch; no ostentatious military decorations, just a simple brass watch chain partly visible at his waist; sleeves rolled neatly to the forearms when working, showing modest white shirt cuffs.
appearance.signature: A rolled telegraph dispatch in one hand and, tucked under the other arm, a worn leather-bound notebook marked by folded chapati impressions along its edges, symbolising his role linking village rumours and electric telegraph reports.

ref_desc: Mark Thornhill is a lean, sun-tanned British magistrate with neat short dark brown hair, cream sun helmet, light khaki tunic coat, dark olive trousers, brown riding boots, and always carries a rolled telegraph dispatch and worn leather notebook in a khaki-and-brown palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body shonen-anime style character of Mark Thornhill: a mid-30s lean British magistrate, oval sun-tanned face, calm grey-blue eyes, short dark brown hair parted left with tidy mid-ear sideburns, wearing a cream colonial sun helmet with a loose brown leather chin strap. His outfit is a mid-1850s light khaki cotton tunic-length coat to mid-thigh with dark brown buttons and two breast pockets over a simple white standing-collar shirt, sleeves rolled neatly to his forearms showing white cuffs; dark olive green straight trousers tucked into mid-calf brown leather riding boots, and a narrow brown leather belt with a small pouch and subtle brass watch chain at the waist. In his hands he holds a rolled telegraph dispatch and tucks a worn leather-bound notebook against his side, edges slightly marked as if pressed by chapatis, conveying his link between village information networks and electric telegraph lines. Show him front-facing in a neutral model-sheet stance, clearly revealing his face, hair, helmet, full costume from head to toe, and the two props, with colours dominated by light khaki, cream, dark olive green, brown leather, and soft white.
